heads.en: ON THE DIGNITY OF THE PRIESTHOOD.

heads.la: CAPUT PRIMUM. Quid sit sacerdotem de sanctis egredi.
heads.en: CHAPTER ONE. What it is for a priest to go out from the holy places.

heads.la: CAPUT II. Quod nobilitas sacerdotum sit vita sancta
heads.en: CHAPTER II. That the nobility of priests is a holy life

heads.la: CAPUT III. Quod sacerdoti vel minima criminis suspicio sit fugienda.
heads.en: CHAPTER III. That even the least suspicion of a crime is to be fled by a priest.

headnotes.la: Cum patriarchae Jacob filio suo Joseph dicat
headnotes.en: Since the patriarch Jacob says to his son Joseph

headnotes.la: …, quae praecesserant, prout Scriptura loquitur, confortarent. Porro autem si David gratiarum promeruit actiones, cum de manubiis, quas Amalecitis abstulerat, senioribus Juda dona transmitteret, dicens
headnotes.en: …hened those that had gone before, as Scripture says. But further, if David deserved thanksgivings when, out of the spoils he had taken from the Amalekites, he sent gifts to the elders of Judah, saying

headnotes.la: …tque depromptas e sanctuario Domini! Verum ut ab occasione corporalium munerum, ad spiritualium benedictionum se sermo dirigat sacramentum; cum apostolus hoc in magna felicitate constituat, quod dicit
headnotes.en: …anctuary of the Lord! But that the discourse may direct itself, from the occasion of bodily gifts, to the mystery of spiritual blessings: since the Apostle sets this among great happiness when he says

headnotes.la: …ae conversationis attollat; et sicut per acceptae dignitatis sublime fastigium caeteris eminet, sic eum prae caeteris vita supereminens, et spiritualium morum splendor exornet. Unde per Moysen dicitur
headnotes.en: …e rest through the lofty pinnacle of the dignity he has received, so a life surpassing the rest, and the splendor of spiritual character, may adorn him beyond the rest. Whence it is said through Moses

headnotes.la: …libutae per evidens sanctae operationis indicium. Qui etiam vestitus sanctis vestibus dicitur, quia dignum est, ut sacerdos pietatis *497* atque justitiae semper induviis adornetur, sicut scriptum est
headnotes.en: …n evidence of holy work. He is also said to be clothed with holy vestments, because it is fitting that the priest be always adorned with the garments of devotion *497* and of justice, as it is written

headnotes.la: …ibetur insuper et ad mortuum ingredi; nimirum ut studeat a malis, quibus anima moritur, pedem caute subtrahere, seseque ab operibus mortuis pervigili sollicitudine custodire. De quibus dicit Apostolus
headnotes.en: …in to a dead man: namely, that he take care warily to withdraw his foot from the evils by which the soul dies, and to guard himself from dead works with ever-wakeful concern. Of which the Apostle says

headnotes.la: … neglectis animarum curis per desideria terrena vagatur. De sanctis egreditur, cum ecclesiastica disciplina postposita, transeuntium causarum negotiis immoderatius implicatur. Ubi mox apte subjungitur
headnotes.en: …arthly desires. He goes out from the holy places when, ecclesiastical discipline set aside, he entangles himself too immoderately in the business of passing affairs. Where there is at once fitly added

headnotes.la: … polluitur, cum sacerdos quilibet per terrena desideria sparsus, causisque saecularibus dissolutus, sacrosanctis altaribus audacter assistere non veretur; cum videlicet fit, quod per prophetam dicitur
headnotes.en: … priest, scattered abroad by earthly desires and dissipated by secular causes, does not fear boldly to stand at the most holy altars; when, namely, that comes to pass which is said through the prophet

headnotes.la: Quamobrem ut Ecclesia, Christi in sua vigere munditia valeat, et obsceno male ministrantium contagio non sordescat, illic adhuc apte subjungitur
headnotes.en: …refore, that the Church of Christ may be strong to flourish in her own cleanness, and may not grow filthy with the obscene contagion of those who minister ill, there is still fitly added in that place

headnotes.la: …delicet, si spurca libidinis, ac luxuriantium vitiorum contaminatione polluitur, ab eodem animarum sponso ferali divortio separetur. Huic sordidae uxori Apostolus libellum repudii dederat, cum dicebat
headnotes.en: …y the filthy defilement of lust and of riotous vices, she be separated by a deadly divorce from that same bridegroom of souls. To this defiled wife the Apostle had given a bill of divorce when he said

headnotes.la: …is uxore non tales liberi procreantur, qui Deo sacrificium offerant, sed potius qui severitatem, et ultionem divinae animadversionis incurrant. Hinc est, quod cum ad Osee prophetam divina voce dicatur
headnotes.en: …tten such children as may offer sacrifice to God, but rather such as incur the severity and vengeance of divine chastisement. Hence it is that, when it is said by the divine voice to the prophet Hosea

headnotes.la: Ille, sicut Scriptura testatur,
headnotes.en: he, as Scripture testifies,

headnotes.la: Quod utique nomen, quamvis prosperum significare videatur, in eo quod interpretatur *semen Dei;* hic tamen *vindictam Dei* et *furorem* sonat, cum protinus subinfertur
headnotes.en: …h name, although it seems to signify something prosperous, in that it is interpreted *the seed of God,* here nevertheless sounds *the vengeance of God* and *fury,* since there is straightway subjoined

headnotes.la: Quod autem hic per Jezrahel, non salus, sive prosperitas, sed Dei potius ira signatur, etiam in hoc innuitur, cum protinus subinfertur
headnotes.en: But that here by Jezrahel not salvation or prosperity, but rather the anger of God is signified, is intimated in this also, since there is straightway subjoined

headnotes.la: …uisquis immundae vitae velut uxori vir jungitur, ejusque male blandientis amplexibus oblectatur, nequit ex ea liberos, qui Deo placeant, gignere; quia nec potest ex amara radice dulcis fructus afferri
headnotes.en: … an unclean life as to a wife , and takes delight in her ill-flattering embraces, cannot beget from her children who may please God; because neither can sweet fruit be brought forth from a bitter root

headnotes.la: …s bonorum operum fructus, divina largiente gratia, germinare. Necesse est ergo ut sacerdotalem sacerdos ducat uxorem, ex qua responsuram paterno generi procreet sobolem. Unde et illic congrue subditur
headnotes.en: …born fruits of good works. It is necessary therefore that a priest take a priestly wife, from whom he may beget offspring that will answer to its father's stock. Whence there too it is fittingly added

headnotes.la: …d in libro Esdrae, cum praemissum sit, de filiis sacerdotum filii Hobia, filii Accos, filii Berzellai, qui accepit de filiabus Berzellai Galaaditis uxorem, et vocatum est nomen eorum, protinus additur
headnotes.en: …he priests — the sons of Hobia, the sons of Accos, the sons of Berzellai, who took a wife of the daughters of Berzellai the Galaadite, and their name was called after them — there is straightway added

headnotes.la: … canonicae vigor expellat. Nobilem ergo necesse est esse Ecclesiae sacerdotem, ut qui minister est Domini, erubescat se servum esse peccati. Ad quam nobilitatem nos ille provexit, de quo Apostolus ait
headnotes.en: …hood *499*. The priest of the Church must therefore be noble, so that he who is the minister of the Lord may blush to be the slave of sin. To which nobility he has advanced us of whom the Apostle says

headnotes.la: de quo per Joannem dicitur
headnotes.en: of whom it is said through John

headnotes.la: Hanc autem munditiam, ut sacerdos in se valeat prae caeteris possidere, stigma sanguinis Christi studeat in se signanter exprimere; sicut dicit Apostolus
headnotes.en: But that the priest may be able to possess this cleanness in himself beyond the rest, let him take pains to express in himself, in a marked way, the brand of the blood of Christ; as the Apostle says

headnotes.la: …, quid per hoc, nisi boni operis designatur extremum? Nimirum, ut omne bonum, quod incipimus, perseveranter etiam usque ad felicem terminum perducamus. Hinc est, quod Israelitico populo divina vox ait
headnotes.en: …y this but the end of a good work? Namely, that every good which we begin we should also perseveringly carry through even to a happy end. Hence it is that the divine voice says to the people of Israel

headnotes.la: In quibus utique verbis patenter exprimitur, quod figuratur in membris
headnotes.en: In which words there is plainly expressed what is figured in the members

headnotes.la: ecce sanguis arietis immolati rubet in aure sacerdotis. Quod vero sequitur,
headnotes.en: behold, the blood of the sacrificed ram grows red on the ear of the priest. But what follows,

headnotes.la: ecce manus operantis. Quod autem postremo subjungitur,
headnotes.en: behold the hand of one at work. And what is subjoined last,

headnotes.la: …s titulorum insignibus jubetur adornatus incedere, seseque sequentibus ecclesiasticae militiae cuneis sanguinis et crucis Christi debeat vexilla praeferre. Hoc figurabat Zacharias propheta cum diceret
headnotes.en: …f honor, and ought to carry before him the banners of the blood and of the cross of Christ for the squadrons of the ecclesiastical soldiery that follow. This the prophet Zacharias figured when he said

headnotes.la: …II)]. Sicut enim quatuor illic erant litterae, ita nihilominus quatuor sunt crucis cornua quadrifidi orbis partes amplectentia. Hanc sacerdos portabat in gloriam et decorem; quoniam et Apostolus dicit
headnotes.en: …there were four letters there, so none the less are there four horns of the cross, embracing the parts of the fourfold world. This the priest bore for glory and for beauty; since the Apostle also says

headnotes.la: …andae mysterium scriptum est, quoniam et Elias [n: (IV Reg. II)], et Joannes Baptista zonas pelliceas habebant circa lumbos suos [n: (Matth. III)]. De Salvatore vero nostro Joannes in Apocalypsi dicit
headnotes.en: …y of bearing the cross that it is written that both Elias [n: (IV Reg. II)] and John the Baptist had leathern girdles about their loins [n: (Matth. III)]. But of our Savior John says in the Apocalypse

headnotes.la: Constat autem, quia inter utramque mamillam cor hominis constituitur. Unde sponsa dicit in Canticis
headnotes.en: Now it is agreed that between the two breasts the heart of man is set. Whence the bride says in the Canticles

headnotes.la: …us infestantium cogitationum impetus infoederabili certamine dimicamus. Tunc itaque fiet quod illic sequitur; mox enim ut sanctum Domini super frenum equi futurum propheta praemisit, praesto subjunxit
headnotes.en: …arassing thoughts. And so then will come to pass what follows there; for as soon as the prophet had premised that the holy thing of the Lord would be upon the bridle of the horse, he at once subjoined

headnotes.la: Lebetes plane in phialas verti; et zonam auream circa mamillas haberi praecipiebat Dominus in Evangelio, cum dicebat
headnotes.en: Plainly the Lord was commanding in the Gospel that caldrons be turned into bowls, and that a golden girdle be had about the breasts, when he said

headnotes.la: …intellige. Lebetes plane illorum erant pectora, qui suspirabant pisces Aegypti, qui nauseantes manna, esuriebant pepones, inhiabant caepas et allia. An lebetes non erant, qui ferventes clamabant, quia
headnotes.en: …y, were the breasts of those who sighed after the fish of Egypt, who, sick of the manna, hungered for melons and gaped after onions and garlic. Or were they not caldrons, who cried out, seething, that
